summary: NT-proBNP is released when heart chambers are stretched by pressure or volume. Its main strength is what a normal result means: it makes heart failure very unlikely, which is why it is used to decide who needs an echocardiogram.
what_it_measures: The concentration of N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide in blood, reported in pg/mL.

reference_ranges.note: heart failure unlikely below this in the non-acute setting

interpretations.meaning: A raised NT-proBNP suggests the heart is under strain and warrants an echocardiogram. It also rises with age, kidney impairment and atrial fibrillation.
typical_next_steps: referral timeframe guided by how high the value is

when_to_seek_help: New or worsening breathlessness, especially lying flat or with swollen ankles, should be assessed by a doctor promptly.
approved_by: Demo dataset (illustrative values, not for clinical use)
